Alex: Quick update — priorities for the week: 1) finalize Dedicated SLA wording and thresholds, 2) greenlight EU burst capacity for Dedicated, 3) tighten default data retention for logs and traces. Please scan the asks below.
Priya: Noted. On roadmap: canary for multi-model routing is scheduled Wednesday. Need PM review on routing policy Alex mentioned (including fallback heuristics).
Sam: From infra — we'll provision 2 extra p4d nodes for staging to validate SLA and load tests. ETA Tue EOD. Also suggest nightly bake for canary traffic.
Jordan: Ops note: DR drill Wed 10:00 UTC; expect brief tiered failover. @eng-sre please confirm runbooks and pager schedules.
Lina: Security: the proposed retention defaults (logs 90d, traces 30d, metrics 365d). Exceptions require documented SSO justification and audit approval. Opening PR to infra-policy repo now.
Alex: Decision: adopt 90/30/365 defaults, product teams may request exceptions with SSO justification and security sign-off. Approve canary Wednesday; if key metrics (latency, error-rate, regen-quality) look good, we'll proceed with gradual rollout Thursday.
Priya: Two follow-ups: 1) create evals for routing quality against current prompt set, 2) update Dedicated docs + pricing blurb for burst behavior and SLAs.
Sam: Tagging cost owners for the extra nodes. One ask: any objections to applying a temporary CPU cap on non-prod GPU instances to reduce noisy-neighbor variance?
Alex: Go ahead with the CPU cap plan; keep me posted on perf regressions. Thanks.
OpsBot: Deploy scheduled — canary routing rollout v0.9 -> staging: 2026-03-25 09:00 UTC. Automated health check will run for 6 hours.
Jordan: I'll publish updated SLA draft by EOD Monday and share the PR link here.
Alex: Thanks team. Short sync tomorrow 11:00 to confirm readiness. :rocket: :spiral_calendar_pad:
